summary: Cow Knob tower on the Virginia-West Virginia line in George Washington NF: 45-foot steel tower with a 14 by 14 foot cab, built 1932, removed before 1993, sold at auction.

facts.design: 45-foot steel tower with a 14 by 14 foot wooden cab
facts.status_note: Removed before 1993 and sold at auction to a local buyer

events.note: 45-foot steel tower with a 14 by 14 foot wooden cab
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged steel structure about 45 feet high with a 14-foot square wooden house on top
Register says removed before 1993; the year is an upper bound (see corrections). Sold at auction to a local from the Rockingham County area, with hopes of rebuilding

evidence.supports: built in 1932 as a 45-foot steel tower with a 14 by 14 foot wooden cab
evidence.quote: It was built in 1932 as a 45-foot steel tower with a 14'x14' wooden cab.

evidence.supports: sold at auction to a local from the Rockingham County area, hopes of rebuilding
evidence.quote: It was sold at auction to a local from the Rockingham County area with hopes of one day rebuilding it.
It could be seen from US 33.

evidence.supports: one of the towers on the Virginia/West Virginia line
evidence.quote: Cow Knob tower was one of the many towers on the Virginia/West Virginia state line.

evidence.supports: in the George Washington National Forest
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
1956 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1956 (WRH)

evidence.supports: four-legged steel structure with a 14-foot square wooden house on top, about 45 feet high
evidence.quote: THE LOOKOUT IS A FOUR LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE WITH A 14 FOOT SQUARE WOODEN HOUSE ON TOP. IT IS ABOUT 45 FEET HIGH.

evidence.supports: on the highest part of Cow Knob in the Shenandoah Mountains, on the Virginia-West Virginia line
evidence.quote: ON THE HIGHEST PART OF COW KNOB IN THE SHENANDOAH MOUNTAINS AND ON THE VIRGINIA-WEST VIRGINIA LINE.

corrections.why: The Register gives a 45-foot tower and the 1956 station description says about 45 feet high; 45 feet is about 13.7 m. 4.3 m is about 14 feet.
The Register says removed before 1993. 1993 is an upper bound, not the removal year.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both lookout registers that carry the same 1932 build and 1956 description. No staffing, fire, or auction-era sources found in two searches. No source describes the site today, and access is unknown, so no access key is given. Brief height 4.3 m is wrong. The story says plainly that no source describes what remains.
